category: premium file host with a webmaster-gated free tier and pay-per-download programme

free_tier.stated: "Deleted after 3 days. Sign up to store longer." The free path accepts uploads but keeps them three days; the site also says file upload privileges are for verified webmasters.
free_tier.notes: Three days is the shortest free retention met.

per_object_cap.stated: "Upload Large Files 110GB" - the headline figure, 110 GB per file.
per_object_cap.notes: 110 GB taken in the site's own decimal-free phrasing; stored above as 110 x 1024^3. The page does not say whether the 110 GB applies to the free path or to Premium.

retention.stated: Anonymous uploads: 'Deleted after 3 days'. Registered accounts 'store longer' - the number is not printed.

egress.terms: Downloads are served from a CDN: 'Multi-region with CDN for fast global delivery'. Premium advertises 'unlimited bandwidth'. No allowance is printed for the free path.

interface_detail: A web upload form at /upload with no documented API on the pages read. A referral URL pattern exists (/api/ref/<code>) which is a marketing link, not an endpoint.
tooling: Browser upload only as read. For a user that is a tooling note, not a verdict: the form is a POST and could be driven by a script.
chaining: Not a storage answer at three days. Its place in the corpus is as a price reference: EUR/USD 20 per TB-month for storage is the shape of a host that sells capacity, against hosts here that give it away and monetise the player instead.

limits.value: upload privileges are for 'verified webmasters with established websites and significant traffic', by application
additional storage at USD 20 per TB per month for non-webmaster accounts

limits_note: Two gates stack: the upload right is reviewed, and the free retention is three days. A client that is not a webmaster cannot use this as storage at any price below USD 20/TB-month.
binding_note: Before any byte or day can bind, the account has to be approved as a webmaster. At 1 TiB a month an unapproved account never reaches a quota question, and an approved one hits the 3-day retention on the free path.

identity_cost.detail: Registration is free, but the upload right needs a review of the applicant's website: 'FileQ provides file upload privileges exclusively to verified webmasters with established websites and significant traffic'.

reliability_note: A hosting service whose free tier deletes in three days and whose upload right is discretionary: both are account decisions, so both can change without a pricing page changing. The 110 GB figure is a headline with no stated tier attached.
confidence_note: The 3-day retention, the 110 GB headline, the webmaster gate and the USD 20/TB price were read on the vendor's pages. Not established: whether 110 GB applies to free or paid, and what an account's retention actually is.

evidence.proved: 'Upload Large Files 110GB', 'Deleted after 3 days. Sign up to store longer.', and the webmaster-oriented pitch
'Additional Storage: $20 per TB monthly for non-webmaster accounts', the webmaster-only upload policy, 'unlimited bandwidth' on premium, and PPD on Pro and Team

price_per_tb_month: USD 20 per TB-month of additional storage

extras.referral_pattern: /api/ref/<code> is a referral link, not an API endpoint
